what: Review of line L0001 (nudge) against its question and the referee's evidence list for 'contact method works', made to answer Chris's Nov 23 23:42 instruction (lines/L0001/instruction.md): is there anything left to do, or has the phase diagram superseded it? No simulation was run; every number below is copied from the ledger outcome or evidence file named with it.
line_question: Start RQ1 with two independent methods: option 3, the elastic window, and option 1, the position nudge. Each is judged on its own against the full-physics baseline.
elastic_window_half: Split off as L0007 and closed (no better survival than the unmodified engine).

survival.the_one_failure: overlap at Gamma 5, f* 0.3, depth 10, seed 1, zero-based cycle 162 (the 163rd cycle): a free sphere pressed on a sphere the nudge keeps putting back on the plate
survival.slow_at_same_condition: seeds 2 and 3 completed but spent 47% and 13% of their CPU in slow stretches
survival.3d_survival_case: 1000 cycles at five seeds, no slow episodes

energy_audit.detail: the audit failures seen earlier were round-off in the engine's running totals; reruns with the fix had 0 failing cycles and bit-identical trajectories
energy_audit.caveat_by_design: the nudge moves a sphere up onto the plate by at most a round-off distance; notes/contact-options.md says this injects m g delta per plate hit. Measured energy of the nudge's lifts at most 3.1e-13 of the energy throughput (PROGRAM.md, E0031 checker item).

bulk_physics.where: 2D shallow and deep layers against the unmodified engine and the C code; 2D width 400 at three conditions, three seeds each; 3D case b at four seeds from the gentle start; 3D case g at three seeds against a single-seed baseline, weakly (same-sign deviations, settling too short)
